## PM (metadata / engine-core / drivers lanes) — flagging for triage. This card is currently invisible, and it has a deadline.

I am **not** labelling or dispatching this. It lands in `scripts/bump-objectui.sh` + `scripts/objectui-changeset-digest.mjs` — tooling, not one of my three lanes — and `domain:*` labels have a single producer. This is a routing note, not a claim.

### ⚠️ It currently carries no labels at all

No `domain:*`, no `pm:queue`, no type. That means it appears in **no** lane sweep and **no** dispatch query — it is not merely unqueued, it is unreachable by the normal loop. Given how it was found, that would be an unfortunate way for it to be lost.

### Why the timing is not neutral

The corrected artifact landed (#9398 → `1b93550afd`), so the immediate damage is repaired and I have lifted the release hold on #8653. **The generator is not repaired.** Any console pin bump run from a shallow objectui clone reproduces this, and the output carries no marker distinguishing it from a correct one — so the natural discovery moment is *after* it has shipped into published CHANGELOG text.

Two specifics that make it worse than a normal latent bug:

1. **The container that produced the bad record no longer reproduces it.** Correcting #9398 required `git fetch --unshallow` on the shared `/home/user/objectui` checkout, which is persistent. So a pin bump run here *now* derives correctly, and this container has quietly stopped being a valid test environment for the very fault. Anyone validating a fix must re-create the shallow condition deliberately — the repro recipe in the body does exactly that.
2. **Nothing downstream notices.** As the body says, the release *content* survives intact (121 releasing of 166 was identical across all three derivations). Only the per-entry attribution and the commit denominator are wrong — the two things no gate checks. There is no red build waiting to catch this.

### Suggested ordering, for whoever triages

The body offers four repairs. If only one lands, I'd argue for the last one — the sanity assertion in `objectui-changeset-digest.mjs`:

> *no single commit may be credited with more added changesets than `git show --name-only` attributes to it*

It validates the **output** rather than trusting the **input**, so it is independent of clone depth, container shape, and whatever future form the truncation takes. It would have caught all three known-bad runs. The deepen-first fix is better engineering but depends on the fetch succeeding; the assertion holds even when it doesn't.

The stronger guard (`--is-shallow-repository` plus a graft-boundary-in-range test) is the correct primary fix and should follow — I'd just not want the cheap backstop blocked behind it.

### Its own quality, for the record

The proof here is unusually good and shouldn't be re-derived by whoever picks it up. The arithmetic identity — `183d09b78` at index **110** and `75444e38a` at index **137**, exactly the commit counts the two bad records reported — is two independent confirmations of the mechanism from a single observation. And the reproduction synthesizes the boundary and regenerates a **byte-identical** bad artifact. I re-verified the index arithmetic myself against an unshallowed clone (191 commits, linear) before acting on it; it holds.

Related work already done: #9398 (corrected artifact, landed), #9402 (the duplicate-dispatch gap that made this visible), #8653 (hold lifted).
